title: Real Estate
sub: One sheet per property. Houses, condos, mobile homes, rental property, and vacant land.

matter.label: Date of death or appointment
matter.hint: This is the valuation date for the inventory.

options.label: Secure the property: keys in hand, doors and windows locked
Confirm insurance is active and the insurer knows the home is vacant
Check for people or animals inside before anyone leaves
Photograph or video every room before anything is moved
Secure firearms, cash, jewelry, medications, and original documents (attorney directs how)
Keep heat on in cold months or confirm the home is winterized

rows.label: Title holder(s), exactly as on the deed

rows.html: Before the first visit: pull the county auditor and recorder records. A recorded transfer-on-death affidavit (R.C. 5302.22) or survivorship deed can mean the property passes outside probate. Flag it to the attorney before anything else is planned.

rows.label: How many keys, and where they're kept
Garage opener, mailbox, gate, outbuilding keys
Where the lockbox code is kept (not the code)
Neighbor or contact watching the property (name and phone)
Security deposit amount and who holds it
Could the ward return home?
rows.hint: Guardianship only. This changes the whole plan for the house.

rows.html: Never tell an occupant to leave, change the locks on an occupied home, or promise anyone they can stay. Get the facts and bring them to the attorney. In an estate, a surviving spouse may have a right to remain in the home (R.C. 2106.10).

rows.label: Insurer told the home is vacant
Named insured is the estate / guardianship

rows.html: Whose name the insurance is in: always the estate or the guardianship. Never the attorney personally, never Gasper Legal, never a staff member. A fiduciary can be named only in their fiduciary capacity, for example "Jane Doe, Administrator of the Estate of John Doe," so they carry no personal responsibility. If a policy lists anyone individually, flag it to the attorney.
Many homeowner policies restrict or drop coverage once a home sits vacant for a set period, often 30 to 60 days. Get the agent's answer in writing and calendar the date.

rows.label: Amount owed and next due date

rows.html: Reverse mortgages come due on a strict timeline after death or a permanent move out. Flag to the attorney the same day you learn of one.

rows.label: Lawn and snow service arranged with
Exterior damage, hazards, trees, drainage, anything else
Repairs needed and rough cost, if known
Where the documents were taken and stored
Family requests for items (note them, promise nothing)
Lienholder / heir consents and service status

rows.html: Do not list the property, sign a listing agreement, or accept an offer until the attorney confirms the court authority is in place.

rows.label: Do we have control of it

rows.text: If not, steps to get control

options.label: Insurance in the estate / guardianship's name
Mail and tax bills sent to the firm

rows.label: Who controls it now, if not us

options.label: Transfer / distribute to next of kin

rows.text: Settled means we are 100% done with this asset. Nothing is left to do and we will never need to touch it again. Usually it has been sold, cashed out, distributed to next of kin, or confirmed as not ours to manage. If any follow-up remains, it is not settled.
